figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 1. Phosphopantetheinylation of PKS ACP domains, catalyzed by Sfp. In path 1, the PKS ACP domains are not efﬁciently phosphopantetheinylated in vivo and, therefore,
are ﬂuorescently labeled in vitro. In path 2, efﬁcient phosphopantetheinylation in vivo blocks ﬂuorescent labeling in vitro.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 2. SDS–PAGE of DEBS proteins containing ﬂuorescently labeled ACP domains scanned on the Typhoon imager. (A) In vitro reaction containing Bodipy–CoA and extracts
from strain BL21 (sfp) (lane 4) and from strain K-207-3 (+sfp) (lane 5). Imager parameters were as follows: 488 nm laser; 520 nm bandpass 40 emission ﬁlter; 470 V PMT.
(B) In vitro reaction containing Alexa647–CoA and extracts from strain BL21 (sfp) (lane 6) and from strain K-207-3 (+sfp) (lane 7). Imager parameters were as follows:
633 nm laser; 570 nm bandpass 30 emission ﬁlter; 470 V PMT. (C) Emission channels from panels A and B displayed simultaneously. (D) Image of the same gel shown in
panels A to C, stained for total protein with SYPRO Red. Image parameters were as follows: 532 nm laser; 610 nm bandpass 30 emission ﬁlter; 490 PMT. The gel shown is
representative of multiple (>3) independent experiments. The high-molecular-weight bands corresponding to DEBS2 (374 kDa), DEBS3 (332 kDa) and module 2 of DEBS1
(164 kDa) are shown. Due to their large sizes, the DEBS proteins are well separated from endogenous E. coli proteins.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 3. (A) SDS–PAGE of Alexa647–CoA-labeled DEBS from BL21 and K-207-3 and
estimation of extent of phosphopantetheinylation of DEBS ACP domains expressed
in K-207-3. (B) The line tool in the ImageQuant software was used to quantify signal
intensities of individual bands. Signal intensities corresponding to DEBS module 2
(mod2), DEBS2 (2), and DEBS3 (3) are indicated (see also Fig. 2), and serial dilutions
of 1% (1:99) and 0.1% (1:999) are shown. The signal intensities from protein bands
derived from the undiluted sample from strain K-207-3 containing Sfp were less
than those from 1:999 diluted sample originating from BL21(DE3) without Sfp.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 4. In vitro ﬂuorescent assay for phosphopantetheinyl transferase, catalyzed by Sfp or NpgA. (A) Image from Typhoon scan. Lanes 2, 3, 7, and 8: NpgA; lanes 4, 5, 9, and 10:
Sfp. Equivalent amounts of NpgA and Sfp were used. Lane 1: BJ 5464 host; lane 2: BJ5464 + YEplovB; lane 3: BJ5464 + 1 copy npgA + YEplovB; lane 4: BJ5464 + YEplovB; lane 5:
BJ5464 + 1 copy sfp + YEplovB; lane 6: protein markers; lane 7: BJ5464 + YEp6MSAS; lane 8: BJ5464 + 1 copy npgA + YEp6MSAS; lane 9: BJ5464 + YEp6MSAS; lane 10:
BJ5464 + 1 copy sfp + YEp6MSAS. The imager parameters were as follows: 488 nm laser; 520 nm bandpass 40 emission ﬁlter; 470 to 525 V PMT. (B) Image of same gel with
Coomassie blue stain. LovB = 335 kDa; 6-MSAS = 190 kDa. The gel shown is representative of multiple (>2) independent experiments.
